1.w: And after five days the high priest Ananias came down with some elders and a certain orator, Tertullus, who made a presentation against Paul to the governor.

2.w: And he having been called, Tertullus began to accuse [him], saying, “Attaining great peace through you, and excellent measures being done to this nation through your foresight,

3.w: in every way and also everywhere, we gladly accept [it], most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.

4.w: But so that I should not be a hindrance to you any longer, I implore you to hear us briefly [in] your kindness.

5.w: For having found this man a pestilence and stirring dissension among all the Jews in the world—also a leader of the sect of the Nazarenes—

6.w: who even attempted to profane the temple, whom we also seized.

8.w: Having examined [him] yourself, you will be able to know from him concerning all these things of which we accuse him.”

9.w: And the Jews also agreed, declaring these things to be so.

10.w: And the governor having motioned to him to speak, Paul answered: “Knowing you as being a judge to this nation for many years, I make a defense cheerfully to the things concerning myself,

11.w: you being able to know that there are to me no more than twelve days since I went up to worship in Jerusalem.

12.w: And neither did they find me reasoning with anyone or making a tumultuous gathering of a crowd in the temple, nor in the synagogues, nor in the city.

13.w: Nor are they able to prove to you [the things] concerning which now they accuse me.

14.w: But I confess this to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I serve the God of our fathers, believing all things throughout the Law and that have been written in the Prophets,

15.w: having a hope in God, which they themselves also await, [that] there is about to be a resurrection both of righteous and of unrighteous.

16.w: In this I myself also strive to have a conscience without offense toward God and men through everything.

17.w: Now after many years, I arrived to bring alms to my nation, and offerings,

18.w: during which they found me purified in the temple, not with a crowd nor with an uproar. But [there are] some Jews from Asia

19.w: who ought to appear before you and to make accusation if they may have anything against me.

20.w: Or let these say themselves any unrighteousness they found in my having stood before the Council,

21.w: other than concerning this one voice in which I cried out standing among them: ‘I am judged by you⁺ this day concerning the resurrection of the dead.’”

22.w: But Felix, having known more precisely the things concerning the Way, put them off, having said, “When Lysias the commander shall have come down, I will examine the things as to you⁺,”

23.w: having commanded the centurion to keep him and to [let him] have ease and not to forbid his own to minister to him.

24.w: Then after some days Felix, having arrived with [his] own wife Drusilla, being a Jewess, sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.

25.w: And [in] his reasoning concerning righteousness and self-control and the coming judgment, Felix, having become frightened, answered, “Be going for the present, and having found opportunity, I will call for you,”

26.w: at the same time also hoping that riches will be given to him by Paul. Therefore also, sending for him often, he was talking with him.

27.w: But two years having been completed, Felix received Porcius Festus [as] successor, and wishing to acquire for himself favor with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.
